purpose: Case-driven verification plan for the Blackwell warp-specialization article. Every case names a frozen fixture and the strongest structural claim that can be made without SM103 execution.

evidence_vector.frontend_or_explicit_input: Whether a Python/API input or explicit IR fixture exists.
evidence_vector.automatic_discovery: Direct evidence for eligibility and automatic partition policy on this shape.
evidence_vector.focused_transform: Direct unit evidence for one or more local pass contracts.
evidence_vector.composed_pipeline: Evidence that multiple passes compose on one frozen IR fixture; this does not imply provenance from a same-named Python source.
evidence_vector.target_lowering: LLVM/PTX checks or locally generated SM103 artifacts.
evidence_vector.runtime_qualification: Same-target launch, numerical, and profiling evidence.
evidence_vector.rule: Axes are independent and unordered. No aggregate maturity score or weakest-link rank is derived from them.

assertion.required: Must be checked and is supported by frozen source/test evidence.
assertion.required-composed: Must be established by an explicitly named composition of frozen source and adjacent focused fixtures; it is not claimed as one fixture's direct FileCheck.
assertion.forbidden: Must be absent for this case.
assertion.advisory: Useful observation only; exact spelling/count is toolchain-sensitive or not covered by the fixture.
assertion.known_gap: Normative structure is expected from the external ISA contract but is absent from the frozen implementation, tests, or artifact; this blocks the corresponding qualification claim without making the compile record itself invalid.
assertion.not_applicable: The selected fixture intentionally stops before this representation.

evidence_kind.inference: Reasoned compile artifact expectation; never a runtime measurement.

recommended_artifacts: TTIR immediately after frontend code generation
TTGIR after each AutomaticWarpSpecialization subpass where the fixture supports it
LLVM-dialect MLIR before and after ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM
LLVM IR, PTX, and cubin when the local CUDA toolchain accepts sm_103
nvdisasm output only as a non-blocking advisory artifact
global_protocol.success_rule: Compile success and required structural checks establish observed implementation behavior. A known_gap remains a first-class failed qualification axis even when ptxas accepts the artifact; no compile-only result establishes numerical correctness, memory-model correctness, occupancy, latency hiding, or speedup.
global_protocol.sass_rule: No exact SASS mnemonic is a required assertion in compile-only mode. Record toolchain version and preserve output if available.

cases.evidence_vector_note: The case proves compiler-IR lifecycle and erase boundaries from source, local pass traces, and focused lowering checks, not from a composite CLEAN-NOT nvws.* assertion; it does not prove hardware execution or runtime behavior.
limitations: The passes rely on internal pipeline invariants and selected assert/unreachable paths rather than a dialect-wide ConversionTarget proof.

ArefCreate does not verify non-empty or unique ownership; exit completion arrays/token pairing and ArefBuffer token provenance, result arity, and precise result types are protocol invariants, with view count checked only by a lowering assert.

Zero-region/no-result warp_group passes verification although LowerWarpGroup indexes the first group; positive/power-of-two numWarps, yield/result type equality, and terminator placement outside a result-bearing first region are not fully checked. Worker lowering discards the input terminator and creates warp_return.

The composite automatic-warp-specialization CLEAN prefix checks ttg.partition metadata and the internal tag, not nvws.* residue; the full-trace observation therefore remains a separate evidence object.
The legacy !nvws.token family is classified separately and is not exercised by current AutomaticWS.
No direct negative matrix exists for all warp_group verifier and AsyncOp combinations.
